title: Quick Revision: Matter in Our Surroundings

bullets: Particles of matter have spaces between them, are continuously moving, and attract each other.
Diffusion (e.g. the smell of hot food spreading) shows that particles move; it is faster at higher temperature.

table: Takes the shape of the container

bullets: **Melting point** of ice: 273 K (0 °C). **Boiling point** of water: 373 K (100 °C). Temperature stays constant during a change of state.
**Latent heat** is the heat used to change the state without raising the temperature (latent heat of fusion; of vaporisation).
**Sublimation:** solid changes directly into gas, e.g. camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride. The reverse is called deposition.
Increasing pressure and lowering temperature can turn a gas into a liquid. Solid CO_{2} is called dry ice.

box: **Evaporation** happens at any temperature below the boiling point, at the surface. It increases with surface area, temperature and wind speed, and **decreases with humidity**. Evaporation causes **cooling**.

bullets: Confusing evaporation (surface, any temperature) with boiling (whole liquid, fixed temperature).
Writing °K. The unit is just K.

blocks.p: 1. Convert 25 °C to the Kelvin scale, and 373 K to °C.
2. Why do we feel cool after sweating, and why is this slower on a humid day?
